findings.claim: statedPartners unions partner rows across every cited finding under one comparable() key, so a #477 finding's order is credited as stated through ANOTHER finding's rows. That makes the new statedPartners javadoc, the ADR Decision 100 amendment and the README exception wrong when they say #477's findings' orders are 'stated only by its display'.
findings.evidence: Throwaway @Test added to CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (reusing its OverShippedData: shipped KB, real injector, real search()), then restored with git checkout. Orders Nevirapine J05AG01, Rifampicin J04AB02, 'Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin' J04AM05; question 'Can I give her alprazolam?'. The injector wrote [6] partners=[Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin] rows=[[6038]] (isoniazid rule) and [8] (#477 finding) partners=[Rifampicin, Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin] rows=[[],[]]. An answer citing [5][6][7][8] and naming only 'isoniazid' gave FindingPartnerCoverage{named=5, stated=3}: Nevirapine, plus the combo counted twice, once for [6] and once for the #477 finding [8], which carries no rows of its own. Positive control: with the prose-rule arm disabled (`false && validator != null` in statedPartners, restored afterwards) the same answer gave stated=1. ordersOfOneSubstanceAreNotStatedByThatSubstancesName stays green because its arrangement has no rule finding that shares a printed order with the #477 finding. Fix: decide statedness per (finding, partner) from that finding's own rows, or correct the three docs to describe the union.

findings.claim: When a rule chip's printed partner is a combination prescription's display (the #339 order rung), the chip's rows are the single constituent the rule is about. An answer naming that one constituent now states the whole combination order and suppresses the 'not named above' sentence. This residue runs toward silence and is not listed among the 'other direction' residues in README, ChartSearchService.FindingPartnerCoverage or ADR Decision 100. Is it intended?
findings.evidence: Throwaway @Test added to CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (reusing its OverShippedData: shipped KB, real injector, real search()), then restored with git checkout. Orders Nevirapine J05AG01 and 'Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin' J04AM05; alprazolam question. The findings were [5] partners=[Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin] rows=[[6038]] and [6] same partner rows=[[9384]]. An answer naming only 'rifampicin' (and separately only 'isoniazid') was returned unchanged with FindingPartnerCoverage{named=3, stated=3}. The same answers with the prose-rule arm disabled appended 'Also covered by those findings and not named above: active order Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin.' with stated=1. The docs read are README.md:555 and ChartSearchService.java:713-726; their 'opposite direction' lists name only substring containment and the shared-alias case. One alternative avoids this residue for the issue's own case: match against the display of the order the partner was bridged to (her order is displayed 'Rifampicin'), carried per partner.

verdict: Close to mergeable. It fixes #555's reported case on both paths and on the screening and merged findings. The biggest reason to hold it is that the per-key row union contradicts the PR's own documented guarantee about #477 findings (F1), and that combination-order residue toward silence is undocumented (F2).
